structured_output.summary: The change implements String.prototype.trim and a TrimString helper in the ticket's file only. Steps follow the spec: this value is passed through, RequireObjectCoercible runs before ToString, and the ? propagation is kept. The whitespace set matches the spec's WhiteSpace plus LineTerminator union: TAB, VT, FF, SP, NBSP, ZWNBSP, the Zs code points (U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000), LF, CR, LS and PS. U+180E is correctly excluded. Every member is in the BMP, so per-code-unit checks are sufficient. The start and end loops are bounded correctly, including the all-whitespace case. The four remaining failures are not-implemented errors from other built-ins (Array.prototype.toString, RegExp), which is the correct behaviour. No test-specific branches, no swallowed errors, no fabricated values.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: No defects found. The diff is sound as written. Minor, non-blocking: TrimWhere::Start and TrimWhere::End are only reached through trim_string, so the other built-ins that need TrimString will use them. The section number in the doc comment (§22.1.3.35.1) could not be verified against the pinned spec and is cosmetic only.
